newsitem.title: INDIA: Year-end support to boost gold demand to 95 high.
newsitem.headline: Year-end support to boost gold demand to 95 high.

text.p: Strong last-quarter support for gold will push up 1996 demand for the precious metal to match the all-time high of 2,725 tonnes achieved in 1995, an official of the World Gold Council said on Thursday.

"Total demand in 1996 is very very close to all-time records achieved last year," George Milling-Stanley, manager (Gold Market Analysis) for the WGC, told an international seminar in the Indian capital.
"The fourth quarter demand is traditionally strong," Milling-Stanley added.
He said global gold demand in the first three quarters of 1996 had been only slightly lower than in 1995, and the shortfall would be made up in the last quarter of 1996.
"The demand in the first three quarters of 1996 was only three percent lower compared to 1995, and the fourth quarter peak demand should make it up," Milling-Stanley said.
However, Milling-Stanley could not predict price behaviour in the last quarter.
In 1994, global demand for the precious metal was 2,460.1 tonnes, he added.
